newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey county to charge jail inmates "rent".
newsitem.headline: New Jersey county to charge jail inmates "rent".

text.p: Inmates of the Ocean County Jail will soon be paying more than their debt to society.
The Board of Freeholders voted on Wednesday to charge them $200 for the first 10 days of their sentence and $10 a day after that.
"It's time we showed that we are serious about crime," Freeholder Jack Kelly said. Officials estimate that the plan will defray 5 percent to 6 percent of the cost of keeping criminals locked up.
Kelly said that if inmates were broke, the county would take legal action to ensure that they paid what they owed after their release.
County jails in New Jersey hold people serving terms of up to one year for such violations as drunken driving, creating public disorder and shoplifting.
The American Civil Liberties Union has warned the freeholders it will challenge as "double punishment" any attempt to collect the fees from prisoners sentenced before the law was passed.
But David Rocah, a staff attorney with the group's New Jersey chapter, pointed out a problem that could threaten the scheme, along with a similar one planned by Camden County.
"It costs more to collect these fees from indigent inmates than jurisdictions usually realise by the effort," he said.
